title: Make land --pr judge the PR's current head and refuse extra commits
summary: `athena land --pr` will ask the host for the pull request's current head and judge that head's checks. It will merge guarded by that head, and it will never force-replace a newer head with the job's commit. Until the records-history build (D111) lands, it refuses whenever the head is anything other than the job's landing commit, declared intervention or not, and names the extra commits. The audience is the user running land after pushing a fix to the PR.

defaults_applied.how: Tests added in gh.rs; cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
Criteria run land_pr against a fake host and check the merge guard, the refusal and the absence of a force-replace.
The check lookup is keyed to the PR's current head, not patched for one case.
Docs and refusal messages are written for an outside reader.
An independent verifier runs the named test commands.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: land --pr must merge a PR whose head was fixed after landing, without the user bypassing land. It must refuse any head that is not the job's landing commit.
The user's reply to the earlier reading overrides the original 'declared intervention' exception: the refusal covers all extra commits until D111 lands.
The code is in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs (land_pr, wait_for_checks, PrLink, replace_head); the exact host trait method for reading the PR head may need adding.
The request text that mentions PR #149 describes a past failure; it needs no change outside land.
The refusal message may mention D111 by name, since the user named it.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test shows that when the PR's current head is not the job's landing commit, land_pr refuses to merge. The error names every extra commit, covers declared interventions as well as undeclared ones, and tells the user why (a squash of the landing plus a later commit is not a valid landing until D111). The host's merge endpoint is not called. Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core gh::`.

A test shows that when the PR head is the job's landing commit and its checks are green, land_pr merges guarded by that head. A second test shows that the PR's checks, not the stale commit's, are what gets reported after the PR is fixed and its head is back at the landing commit. Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core gh::`.
A test shows land_pr never calls the remote's replace/force-push when the remote head differs from, or descends from, the job's commit. Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core gh::`.

The existing external_calls tests (retries, persistent 500s) and the display tests for the land --pr report still pass. Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli`. `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

The module and function docs state that checks and the merge guard are keyed to the PR's current head. The refusal message names each extra commit and points to the D111 limitation. The CHANGELOG entry, if added, describes the fix for an outside reader.
No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) changes.

out_of_scope: Changing spec checker behavior in xtask
departures: The change is somewhat larger than average because it touches the host trait and fakes.
